Synopsis:
Scyre, Mortach of Kelemvor, has been told that a little girl is practicing Necromancy in the graveyard. This is when you catch up to them both, and you get one last chance to intervene. In this dialogue you can encourage Nina to stop her Necromancy, threaten her, or even convince her to try again later.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_PriestessAndNecromancer.json: You arrive in the graveyard with Mortarch Gracie Scyre catching a little girl in the act of necromancy — this is the final moment to stop her. The child, Nina Dortmell, is grieving her older brother Garret (murdered by the serial killer Dolor) and secretly tried to raise him at his grave; she asked the player to keep watch and has genuine but inexperienced power, and her ritual has already faltered. Gracie Scyre is a gentle, devout priestess of Kelemvor who comforts the bereaved but firmly insists necromancy “twists” death and will condemn or expel anyone who uses it here. The player can side with Scyre and discourage Nina, threaten consequences, or soothe and delay her attempt (samples show both comforting and more permissive responses); wider threats in the city exist but do not affect this immediate exchange.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KelemvorPriestess.json: The exchange takes place in the graveyard under Mortarch Gracie Scyre’s care; she is a gentle, older priestess of Kelemvor who speaks plainly about death and acts as the cemetery’s shepherd. Off‑screen, the player has been intervening in mourners’ affairs — sometimes helping them, and in at least one case (Nina) using or teaching necromancy to raise a loved one — which provokes Mortarch’s quiet fury. While she calmly offers comfort, teachings, and blessings to those who accept death, she will condemn and expel anyone who uses necromancy to manipulate the grieving or harm innocents, invoking Kelemvor’s judgment. Other city conflicts (Bhaal cult activity, Orin, etc.) may be happening elsewhere but do not change her focus on protecting these hallowed grounds.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KidNecromancer.json: Nina is a small, grieving child secretly attempting to raise her big brother Garret—who was murdered by the serial killer Dolor—at his gravesite. She knows necromancy is forbidden and fears being caught by the Mortarch, so she asks the player to keep watch. She has real magical power but is inexperienced and her ritual falters, leaving her frustrated and desperate. The player may offer practical help (teaching focus or supplying the Raise Undead spell), which changes how the scene can proceed. Other threats noted in the wider cluster (Bhaal cultists, Orin, etc.) exist in the area but aren’t part of this brief graveside exchange.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_Gravekeeper.json: Valmorba is the tired gravekeeper who stays by her little house beside the cemetery, usually sitting or idly pacing; she hides her kindness under weary, gallows‑humour remarks. Lately she's been burying far too many bodies, so she can identify specific plots (for example, M. Kurwin beneath the great willow) and will repeat a curt condolence when she recognises a returning visitor. Players can ask her for a shovel — she'll either lend one or tell you where she keeps hers — but she’ll scold you if you’ve been digging up graves yourself (alternate lines when she’s already met you). She also has lines about the recent killings in Baldur’s Gate (with different branches if the murders have been solved) and may acknowledge local trouble like kobold looters if you’ve encountered them.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_BuriedMan.json: Gothric Rillyn has just pulled himself out of a shallow grave after being buried alive — he was muffled and yelling beneath the dirt and the player (or the player’s party) dug him out off‑screen. He admits he tried to steal from a “baldy” (the man who buried him), and he snipes at that man’s self‑styled title “Stone Lord,” even calling him “Stone Shite.” The lines imply the bald man is Minsc, who in other scenes has embraced the Absolute and taken the Stone Lord name, and Gothric keeps his head down until he’s sure Minsc isn’t present in the party. This exchange follows immediately after Gothric dusts himself off and regains his breath.
